description: Firecracker-internal identifier. Used in URLs (PUT /network-interfaces/{iface_id}) and MMDS network_interfaces[] lists. NOT visible inside the guest — guest names its own interfaces (typically eth0, eth1...).

Host TAP interface name (must already exist). Firecracker opens /dev/net/tun and binds via TUNSETIFF. Permission: requires the running uid to have access to the TAP (typically by being in the netdev group or via uid match on tap-creation).
Guest-side MAC address. If null, randomly generated. Convention with default rootfs: encode the guest IP in the last 4 bytes (06:00:AC:10:00:02 ↔ 172.16.0.2).
Token-bucket capacity in bytes. Bucket fills at refill_time interval to this maximum.
Time in milliseconds to refill the bucket from empty to full. Throughput = size / (refill_time/1000) bytes/sec at sustained rate.
Optional one-shot extra capacity available at startup. Lets a guest burst once above the steady-state limit (e.g., for initial download). Once consumed, never refills.
Operations-per-period bucket capacity. For network: operations = packets. Independent of bandwidth bucket — both must permit the action.
List of network interface iface_ids on which MMDS-destined packets are intercepted. At least one required — without it, MMDS returns 400 on any request.
Forces all MMDS responses to use AWS IMDS plain-text format regardless of Accept header. Lets EC2-IMDS-targeted guest tooling (cloud-init, AWS SDK metadata libs) work unmodified against Firecracker.
Required to be 1 on host for any NAT-based or bridge-based microVM routing. Without it, packets from TAP to physical NIC are dropped at the FORWARD chain.
TAP send queue length on the host. Tunable for high-throughput workloads — too small drops packets; too large adds latency. Set via `ip link set <tap> txqueuelen <N>`.
MMDS protocol version. V1 = simple GET (deprecated, removed in next major); V2 = session-token-required (mimics IMDSv2). Always use V2 for multi-tenant or untrusted guest workloads.
